li.label: learning to shoot
li.description: They let me hold it properly. It's heavier than it looks and louder than it sounds. I hit the target. Near the target.

li.label: a child with a weapon
li.description: There's a child out there with a loaded weapon and the council's blessing. I've started walking behind things.

li.label: told I'm too little
li.description: Everyone says wait until I'm older. I am older. I get older every single day and nobody notices.

li.label: went out with the hunters
li.description: I carried the bag. It was heavy and it smelled and something in it was still warm. Best day ever.

li.label: minding a child on the hunt
li.description: Spent all day whispering "stay down" to someone who would not stay down. Everything for a mile heard every word.

li.label: proved them wrong
li.description: They said I was too little. The squirrel didn't think so. Well, it doesn't think anything now.

li.label: taught a kid to shoot
li.description: Held it wrong, aimed it wrong, hit the target anyway. I may have cheered. Nobody needs to know I cheered.

li.label: saw what hunting really is
li.description: There was a lot more inside it than I thought, and all of it was warm. I want to grow potatoes now.

li.label: the dead go somewhere nice
li.description: Somewhere warm, with good food and no raiders. I asked if there are dogs. They said probably.

li.label: fairy tales for children
li.description: We told a child the dead go somewhere nice. Then we'll act surprised when the kid grows up believing in luck.

li.label: learned about the worms
li.description: The ground eats you. All of you, even the eyes. I asked about the eyes specifically.

li.label: my worm collection
li.description: I have a jar of worms now. They're going to eat me someday, so it's only polite to get to know them.

li.label: a funeral for a little thing
li.description: We buried a very small animal today, with speeches. Somebody cried. It wasn't me. It was a bit me.

li.label: time wasted on nonsense
li.description: Half the colony stopped work in the middle of the day to stand around making speeches. The fields didn't weed themselves.

li.label: nobody would answer me
li.description: I asked one simple question and every grown-up suddenly had somewhere else to be.

li.label: questions about death at breakfast
li.description: Every meal, the same question. I don't know where the dead go. Nobody knows. Please pass the salt.

li.label: my friend past the wall
li.description: It eats out of my hand now. It has a name. I'm not telling you the name.

li.label: they chased my friend away
li.description: I still put food out every night. It doesn't come anymore. The grown-ups say that's good news.

li.label: they killed my friend
li.description: It used to eat out of my hand. Now it doesn't do anything. I know who did it, and I'm going to remember.

li.label: feeding the wildlife
li.description: Our food, carried out past the wall, into the mouth of something that would eat us if it got hungry enough.

li.label: bitten again
li.description: Same animal, other hand. The council's position seems to be that I've got a spare.

li.label: my animal is fading
li.description: Every morning it takes a little longer to get up. I sit with it. I don't know what else to do.

li.label: took my animal on a last walk
li.description: I walked it out past the walls, slowly, the long way round. I came back alone. It was the kind thing. I keep telling myself that.

li.label: nursing my animal
li.description: Soft food, a warm corner, someone sitting up with it. It's eating again. I'm sleeping again. Mostly.

li.label: dinner got away
li.description: It was right there. Then it was over the wall. I had the water boiling and everything.

li.label: apologized to an animal
li.description: I said sorry to it in front of everyone. It licked itself the whole time.

li.label: my love letter was read aloud
li.description: I wrote it at three in the morning. Everyone heard it at dinner, with voices. I'm never writing anything down again.

li.label: said it out loud
li.description: I stood on a chair and read every word, and my knees shook the whole time. Somebody clapped. I think it was the right somebody.

li.label: a love letter, read from a chair
li.description: Somebody stood on a chair and read a love letter to the whole room. I didn't know people still did that out here.

li.label: my coffin is ready
li.description: It's in the corner of my room. I check the fit some evenings. It's very comforting, and I'm not going to explain why.

li.label: a coffin in the house
li.description: Someone keeps a coffin in their room. Empty, for now. They keep saying "for now."

li.label: heard my own eulogies
li.description: They stood up one by one and said kind things about me, while I was alive to hear it. I didn't know. I really didn't know.

li.label: an honest eulogy
li.description: Everyone said something nice except one, who said something true. Theirs was the longest, and it got applause.

li.label: picked my grave
li.description: A good spot, out of the wind, with a view of the fields. I lay down in it to check. It'll do.

li.label: bolted in at night
li.description: They lock my door from the outside at night, like I'm a prisoner. I'm not a prisoner. I'm just an ambitious sleeper.

li.label: wearing a bell
li.description: I have a bell on my ankle, like livestock. The animals have started treating me as one of their own.

li.label: kept my side deal
li.description: A bit of private trading, a fair price, and the council let me keep it. Some of us have a head for business.

li.label: the colony's hero
li.description: Officially, I'm the one who saved everyone. The story gets better every time I tell it, which is often.

li.label: no hero after all
li.description: I know what I did out there. The witnesses remember it as "a lot of shouting."

li.label: sent word home
li.description: Somewhere a long way off, someone is going to open a letter and find out I'm alive. I hope they sit down first.

li.label: they moved on
li.description: I sent word that I was alive. The answer came back: glad to hear it, remarried, please stop writing.

li.label: couldn't send word home
li.description: Someone out there thinks I'm dead. The council would like to keep it that way.
